findings.title: List feature-gate test no longer pins gate
findings.problem: ensure_read_access now calls is_admin_maintainer_or_auditor, which reads is_admin/is_maintainer/is_auditor and treats non-bool values as False. The service-test fixture _admin_user() (lines 26-30) is a MagicMock that only sets is_admin_or_maintainer=True, so it now fails the read check with 403 'Access denied'. test_list_paginated_rejects_when_feature_disabled (lines 143-149) asserts only code == 403, so it passes whether the 403 comes from the feature gate or the role check (broken verification). The get_for_read_or_404 gate test at 152-158 has the same weakness but is still pinned by test_feature_gate_runs_before_read_role_check (lines 369-375), which asserts the message; nothing pins the list path, and the HTTP auth matrix patches the feature to always enabled (test_cost_centers_router_http_auth.py:107).
findings.impact: This change moved feature-gate responsibility onto each caller (AR-4) and the task requires the gate's order and responses to stay unchanged. If ensure_feature_enabled() is removed from list_paginated or moved after the role check, GET /v1/admin/cost-centers would be served to admins and auditors with the costCenters feature off and no test would fail. Consumer: CostCenterService.list_paginated (src/codemie/service/cost_center_service.py:129-132) behind the cost center list route.
findings.recommendation: Build _admin_user() as a real admin for the new predicate (set is_admin = True and is_maintainer/is_auditor = False as bools, keeping is_admin_or_maintainer = True for ensure_admin), and in test_list_paginated_rejects_when_feature_disabled (and test_get_for_read_or_404_rejects_when_feature_disabled) also assert exc_info.value.message == "Feature not available". Optionally add an admin read-success case for list_paginated/get_for_read_or_404 so the fixture is proven to pass ensure_read_access.
